blocks.text: **The task.** Given a string of words separated by spaces, reverse the order of the words. Trim leading and trailing spaces, and collapse runs of multiple spaces into one.

blocks.code:
"  the sky   is blue  "   ->  "blue is sky the"
"hello world"            ->  "world hello"

blocks.text: Note carefully what is reversed. The **words** change order; the letters inside each word do not. `"the"` stays `"the"`, it does not become `"eht"`.
If you are allowed extra space, this is short — split on whitespace, discard empty pieces, reverse, rejoin:
The regex `\s+` matches one or more whitespace characters, which handles the collapsing requirement for free.
The classic follow-up asks for O(1) space, and the trick is worth knowing because it appears in other rotation problems.

items: **Reverse the entire string.** `"the sky is blue"` becomes `"eulb si yks eht"`. The words are now in the right order — but each is backwards.
**Reverse each word individually.** `"eulb"` becomes `"blue"`, and so on.

blocks.text: Two reversals cancel out *within* each word while leaving the *between*-word ordering flipped. Both steps are the same direct two pointer loop from the earlier lessons, applied to different ranges.
**Time: O(N)** — each character is touched a constant number of times, even with two passes.
**Space: O(N)** for the split version, **O(1)** for the reverse-twice version on a mutable string.
